title: LLM4OM documentation
description: From your first optimization problem to methods, solvers and deployment.
text: LLM4OM turns natural-language problems and data into optimization models and calls solvers to compute plans. Describe requirements, inspect decisions and the modeling process, then revise conditions, compare alternatives and export results. Choose an entry point Entry Starting point Next actions Optimization chat Send a problem or idea Clarify, compute, query, revise and compare scenarios Manual modeling A prepared statement and data Edit inputs, choose settings and follow execution Requirements assistant A developing business idea Create an editable statement and attachments First-time users can complete the production quickstart . To run a service, see installation . title: Your first plan
description: Build, solve and revise a small production plan.
text: Complete a production task from description through modeling, solving, export and revision. The example includes a statement, downloadable data and localized workbench recordings. 1. Prepare a service and preset Open your team service or install one . Choose an available LLM preset; see preset setup to add one. Send the problem in Optimization chat or use manual modeling. This example uses Direct, Pyomo and AUTO to match the recording. 2. Enter the problem Produce nonnegative integer quantities of products A and B. A earns CNY 3 and uses 2 cutting hours and 1 finishing hour per unit. B earns CNY 2 and uses 1 cutting hour and 2 finishing hours per unit. There are 8 hours of each resource. Calculate the production plan with maximum total profit. Start modeling and follow formulation, code and solving. For a data-file version, download JSON or CSV , describe fields and capacities, then run. 3. Review and export The result is A=3, B=2, total profit CNY 13 . Read quantities in Solution and expressions in Formulation/Code. “Export Excel” downloads solution and problem/conditions sheets. Run information retains method, LLM, actual backend, duration and usage. Open the process for individual stages. 4. Revise and compare Request “B at least 3, with other conditions unchanged.” The new result is A=2, B=3, profit 12 . Comparison shows changes from the original. Use Business scenarios to calculate B≥3 and B≥4 together; profits are 12 and 8. See scenario comparison . 5. Follow the recording Production example in the workbench: compute, compare scenarios, edit data. Captions available. Sequence: enter production requirements → inspect profit 13 → enter two scenarios → compare 13, 12 and 8 → open the data editor → edit and save unit profit. Pause, enable captions or use fullscreen. 6. Try it in the docs Change capacity, minimum demand or quantity domain, inspect the plan and download CSV. For your own task, use the requirements assistant or Optimization chat . Try it: resources, integers and infeasibility INTERACTIVE Cutting hours 8 Minimum B 0 3 4 5 Quantity domain Integer: whole units Continuous: divisible units A = 3, B = 2 · 13 Maximize 3A + 2B; 2A + B ≤ 8 and A + 2B ≤ 8. The integer optimum is 13. Download plan CSV Reset A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above.

title: Install and launch
description: Start the platform with Docker Compose or a local Python environment.
text: If you already have a team service address, open it in a browser. To run your own service, Docker Compose installs the workbench, server and solver environment. Prepare an environment Setup Requirements Use Docker Compose Docker, Compose v2.24+, model-service configuration Personal or team service Python service Python 3.11–3.13, uv, Docker, model-service configuration Development or existing Python setup Data lives in a workspace or Compose volume. Choose a machine with persistent storage and access to the model service. Start with Docker Compose git clone https://github.com/Fangziyang0910/LLM4OM.git cd LLM4OM cp .env.example . env chmod 600 . env Edit .env with provider, endpoint, model ID and key; see LLM presets . Then run: docker compose up -d --build docker compose ps After building, open http://localhost:8767 . Initial setup downloads dependencies and builds the Worker. Inspect startup with docker compose logs -f app . Confirm setup in the workbench Check the default preset and backend options. Complete the production quickstart ; the run should retain quantities, formulation, code and stages. Then add attachments or try Optimization chat. Other devices can use the server address. See team deployment for shared access and HTTPS. Start from Python In the cloned repository: uv sync --all-extras uv run llm4om build-worker uv run llm4om serve --workspace runs/web --port 8767 This uses bundled workbench build files and Docker solver sandboxes. runs/web retains history and presets; use --workspace for another location. Maintenance commands Action Command Status docker compose ps Logs docker compose logs -f app Update git pull , then docker compose up -d --build Apply environment changes docker compose up -d app Stop, retaining data volume docker compose down See presets for connections, backends for solver setup and backups for persistent data. Website and platform addresses GitHub Pages serves the website and Docs. The complete platform runs Python and solver services on the configured machine. Team members calculate through that deployed service address.

Result["Status, objective and variables"] Result --> Record["Record, explanation and exports"] Attachments map file names to complete text. build_model(data) parses inputs and returns a native model. The platform executes and retains results. Four configuration objects Term Role Example Method Generation, checking and repair orchestration Direct, TriVAL, BIND LLM preset Service and request configuration Team endpoint and model ID Library Variables, objective and constraints Pyomo, CPMpy, CVXPY Backend Mathematical computation HiGHS, CP-SAT, Gurobi, Ipopt One configuration might be “Feedback Repair + team preset + Pyomo + HiGHS.” Run information retains selections and the actual engine. Four types of model information Information Meaning Production example Parameters Known input values Unit profit and capacity Variables Quantities or choices to determine A and B quantities Objective Expression to minimize or maximize Total profit Constraints Relationships decisions must satisfy Hours and minimum orders Indices extend these objects across products, dates, employees and nodes. Units connect statements, data and result labels. Runs and plans A run contains inputs, settings, steps, formulation, code and execution. A plan is its computed decision result. Revisions create new runs; scenarios connect runs to one baseline. The conversation's current plan determines the basis for questions and changes. Common statuses Status Meaning optimal Optimal result for the current model feasible A feasible plan is available locally_optimal Local result from a native nonlinear path infeasible Current requirements cannot hold together unbounded Objective is unbounded along a feasible direction time_limit Limit reached; inspect retained solution and feedback Execution or validation failure Read the specific stage and feedback Status, values and method validation remain in the run. See results for daily use and methods or solvers for mechanisms and interfaces.

title: Chat Agent
description: Describe a problem, compute a plan and make changes through conversation.
text: Open Chat Agent from “Optimization chat” in the sidebar. Start with an idea, add data, compute a plan, then continue asking questions and revising the same task. Send the first message Choose an LLM preset and describe the problem. Attach CSV, JSON or Excel beside the message. Defaults are Direct, Pyomo and AUTO. Modeling preferences can fix a method and library; messages can also specify them. Plan next week's store staffing. Each day needs at least 3 people. Each employee can work at most 5 days. Every weekend shift needs a supervisor. First check what information is missing from the attachment, then calculate the lowest-cost schedule after we confirm the requirements. Tool execution shows stages and result cards. On desktop, the adjacent workbench displays formulation, code and results. Open a plan's full run page for export. title: Clarify requirements
description: Turn an initial idea into an editable problem statement and data.
text: “Clarify requirements through conversation” develops an initial idea into an editable problem statement and attachments. Use it when the task is known but goals, rules or data need further discussion. Start from a draft or a blank page Existing homepage text and attachments carry into the conversation. You can also start with “Schedule next week's employees across three stores.” The assistant updates the draft and asks for information affecting the next step. Desktop keeps the problem and data beside the assistant. Narrow screens use tabs. Edit the draft directly or switch to Markdown preview. --> Draft["Update editable draft"] Draft --> Edit["User edits and saves"] Edit --> Configure["Choose method, library and preset"] Configure --> Run["Start modeling"] FOLLOW THE EXAMPLE ← Play → 1. Describe the task 2. Add key rules 3. Edit the draft 4. Hand off 1. Describe the task State the objects, time horizon and goal. The assistant organizes the available information. Schedule next week's employees across three stores and control total staffing cost. 2. Add key rules Turn answers into concrete requirements and list the data still needed. At least 3 people per store per day; at most 5 days per person; weekend supervisor. Data: costs, availability and supervisor qualifications. 3. Edit the draft Edit rules, units or wording directly, save, then continue discussing. Allow movement between stores; one store per employee per day. Columns: employee, date, availability, daily cost, supervisor. 4. Hand off Choose settings and start modeling. The method receives the current statement and attachments. Handoff: complete draft + current attachments The run saves this input version. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. A reusable problem structure Task: objects to arrange and time horizon. Decisions: quantities, selections or sequences to determine. Objective: minimum cost, maximum profit or another explicit goal. Rules: individual requirements. Data: file names, field meanings, units and index mappings. Start with the parts you know. Keep costs, times and quantities in explicit units; edit attachment headers to make them clear. Save, search and hand off Leaving the editor saves manual edits; “Save draft” is also available. Sending a message or starting modeling saves pending changes first. Attachments are saved after reading. Search shows queries and sources. Adopt useful business rules into the draft. “Use for modeling” returns the draft to the workbench; settings and modeling are also available directly in the current workspace. Continue working Conversation history retains requirement development; runs retain the handoff statement and data. Unsent text stays in the current browser tab and survives refresh. Stop or retry a turn, then continue refining. Next see data editing and run settings . For clarification and computation in one continuing conversation, use Chat Agent .

title: Upload and edit data
description: Review spreadsheets, fields and units before computing with the full data.
text: Attach CSV, JSON or Excel so generated code can use complete data. Click a file name to inspect fields, edit cells or raw text, and save the attachment to the current problem. Prepare files and descriptions CSV and JSON files support up to 2 MB each. Every Excel worksheet becomes a CSV. Common file-name characters are preserved. Describe file names, fields, units and index mappings in the problem. For production.json , explain that usage rows identify resources and columns identify products, measured in hours per unit, with nonnegative integer production quantities. Download the ready-to-use JSON example and CSV example . What to inspect in the editor Data Example action Headers and units Change “Price” to “Unit profit (CNY)” Identifiers Preserve store IDs such as 001 as text Values Edit costs, demands or available hours Matrix orientation Match rows to warehouses and columns to stores Structure Edit JSON as raw text; switch tables to raw view Tables display 50 rows per page while retaining the complete data. Use raw view above 50 columns. Saving validates CSV quoting and JSON syntax so errors can be corrected in the editor. Try saving and cancelling Edit capacities below. “Save and calculate” creates a revised plan; “Cancel edits” restores saved values. The example retains its original snapshot. Try editing data INTERACTIVE A uses 2 cutting and 1 finishing hour per unit; B uses 1 and 2. Edit capacity, then save to calculate. Resource Capacity Unit Cutting Cutting capacity hours Finishing Finishing capacity hours Save and calculate Cancel edits Saved: 8 / 8 hours → A = 3, B = 2, objective 13. The original snapshot keeps 8 / 8 hours and objective 13. A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. In the workbench, “Save data” applies attachment edits. Modeling uses the current saved inputs; existing runs retain their original data for comparison. title: Configure a run
description: Select a method, modeling library, solver backend and LLM preset.
text: Run settings select the modeling workflow, code library, computation engine and LLM. The homepage shows a configuration summary; open “View run settings” or “Adjust settings” for all options. The four settings Setting Role Production example Method Generation, validation and revision workflow Feedback Repair Modeling library Native model expressed in code Pyomo Backend Computation engine highs or AUTO LLM preset Service used for generation and checking Saved team preset Methods appear on the left; library, backend and preset appear on the right. Choose options and click “Done.” The summary updates, and backend options show availability and reasons. LP/MILP, start with compatible Pyomo or PuLP backends. Inspect CPMpy/OR-Tools for scheduling and logic, CVXPY for convex quadratic structure, and CasADi for smooth nonlinear models. See solver selection . Three configurations to try Task Method Library / backend Inspect First production run Direct Pyomo / AUTO Formulation, quantities and profit Inspect layered business-rule checks TriVAL Mathematically suitable library / AUTO Stage artifacts and validation feedback Large JSON/CSV BIND Pyomo or another compatible library / AUTO Schema and data-reading code Each method article lists current preset parameters, which are saved with runs. Method-specific parameters are set in deployment presets. The UI selects the method and execution environment. Start and follow progress After attachments finish reading, click “Start modeling” or press Ctrl+Enter / Cmd+Enter. The run page displays stages and artifacts. Execution takes place on the server; reopen the link to see progress. Completed runs show status and objective. “Run information” includes actual preset, backend, elapsed time and usage. “Modeling process” expands the stages that used those settings. Batch comparison and next steps Enable “Compare” and select methods or presets to start up to 12 runs. The comparison table aligns settings, results and usage; see method and LLM comparison . title: Review and export results
description: Inspect decisions, the model and solver status, then export the full plan.
text: The run page brings the plan, formulation, code and process together. Start with status and objective, then read the explanation, inspect complete variables or export the result. Navigate from summary to detail Area Content Action Summary Status, objective or failure Jump to formulation or solution Plan explanation Business labels, units and key rules Understand main decisions Solution Groups, lists and two-index matrices Filter values and download CSV Formulation Mathematical expressions Read versions and differences Code Native-library implementation Inspect variables, objective and rules Problem and data Saved statement and attachments Review input snapshot Process Stage calls and feedback Inspect artifacts, errors and revisions Read a concrete result The production example has A=3, B=2 and profit 13. Labels connect quantities to products and units; complete variables retain original names for code inspection. Two-index variables form matrices, useful for employee-by-day or warehouse-by-store plans. List view exposes original names. Filtering helps locate a person, product or time period. Choose an export Export Contents Use Excel: solution sheet Every variable including zeros, labels, units and original names Execution and further analysis Excel: problem and conditions sheet Statement, changes, original input, attachment names, settings and links Trace inputs CSV Complete variable values Spreadsheet or script processing Markdown report Problem, settings, result, formulation, code and notes Reading, archiving and discussion “Export Excel” downloads both sheets. “More → Export report (Markdown)” creates the report. Markdown displays up to 500 nonzero variables; Excel and CSV retain all values. Explanation and complete values The run preset produces labels, units and short explanations; numerical cells read solver values. Explanations use up to 100 nonzero variables. Use the full-variable panel and exports for all data. Explanation language follows the interface at run start. “Run information” shows preset, method, actual backend, time and usage. Find intermediate model executions and feedback in the process view. Continue from a result “Revise requirements” creates a new plan and comparison. “Business scenarios” computes alternatives from the current plan. “Discuss plan” opens the assistant beside the result. Query a schedule first, then request changed conditions. Drag or keyboard-adjust dividers to resize process and assistant panels. Closing a side panel returns the main area to full width. Watch the workflow The recording shows the production result, two minimum-demand scenarios and data editing. Use captions, pause and fullscreen controls. Production example in the workbench: compute, compare scenarios, edit data. Captions available.

title: Discuss a saved plan
description: Explain decisions, calculate totals and continue from the current plan.
text: Click “Discuss plan” on a result to query decisions, calculate metrics, explain the model or create another plan. The assistant sits beside the saved result. Ask a concrete question List Tuesday's scheduled employees and their costs. Total the weekend cost and show the expression. Find product B's quantity and its resource use. The assistant reads the current plan's problem, model and saved values. Variable lookup supports names, groups and pagination over the complete result, useful for both individual decisions and larger totals. headings.label: Create a new plan in one message

title: Revise requirements
description: Change a requirement while keeping the original plan for comparison.
text: “Revise requirements” prepares a changed problem from a saved plan and runs the original modeling configuration again. Both plans are retained, with differences in problem text, objective and decisions. Make one revision Open the original result and choose “Revise requirements.” Enter a specific change, such as “Require B≥3; keep everything else.” Generate the new plan and follow preparation, modeling and solving. Open the plan comparison for objective, variables and text differences. For a complete rewrite, use “More → Edit and run” to return inputs and settings to the editor. title: Compare business scenarios
description: Compare demand or resource changes from one fixed baseline.
text: Business scenarios compute several explicit changes from one saved plan. Compare demand, budgets, capacities, availability or supply conditions. Create a scenario group Choose “Business scenario comparison” below a result. Enter names and changes for 2–6 scenarios. Names identify results; changes become revised problem statements. Each run uses the common inputs and original configuration. Scenario 1: regular order, at least 3 units of B. Scenario 2: larger B order, at least 4 units of B. You can also request several scenarios in one plan-conversation message, then compare the batch. title: Compare methods and LLMs
description: Run different methods or LLMs on the same problem and inspect the results.
text: Method and LLM comparison runs one problem with several configurations and aligns results and usage. Use it to inspect how workflows handle your task and how changing the LLM preset affects the process. Start from run settings Enable “Compare,” select methods or presets, and choose a shared library/backend. Up to 12 runs can start together. After confirming inputs, open the comparison page to follow progress. Try Direct, Feedback Repair and TriVAL with one preset, or hold the method fixed and select two presets. Each row opens its complete run. Reading the table Field Use Method and preset Identify the configuration Status and objective Read computed results Elapsed time Inspect total run duration LLM calls and tokens Understand generation, validation and repair usage Run link Read formulation, code, steps and inputs The page indicates objective agreement. Open a row to inspect a constraint, code version or validation finding. Follow one requirement across runs For production with B≥3: Find B≥3 in the formulation. Find its code constraint and integer domain. Read A, B and profit in results. Inspect whether repair occurred and what changed. This connects call count and elapsed time to actual stages. A workflow may complete directly or find and revise a particular expression. Inputs and records Each run retains the shared input snapshot plus its configuration, process and result. Add tags and notes to record observations across related runs. Concurrency and hourly quotas control startup and queuing. If some runs fail to start, the comparison retains launched items and shows startup information for the rest. See configuration and usage . Continue from the comparison Open a run for inspection, export its report or revise business conditions from it. See methods for mechanisms, parameters and worked examples, and LLM presets for service configuration.

title: Understand infeasibility
description: Use solver evidence to inspect requirements that cannot hold together.
text: An infeasible result means the current requirements cannot hold together in the submitted model. When specific solver evidence is available, the platform connects conflicting constraints to business rules and provides a revision action. Where to inspect it Open “Solution” and “Why infeasible.” Expand the referenced constraints to inspect the expressions or bounds behind an explanation. Formulation and code remain in adjacent tabs. Linear-model diagnosis uses Gurobi IIS; CPMpy uses MUS. Original evidence is retained for tracing business rules to mathematical expressions. A concrete conflict Add B≥5 to production with 8 finishing hours. The relevant expressions are B≥5 , A+2B≤8 and nonnegative quantities. title: History, tags and reports
description: Find related plans, record conclusions and export reports.
text: History connects requirement drafts, modeling runs, revisions and comparisons. Tags and notes capture decisions; fixed links and reports support team discussion and archiving. Find related task records The sidebar groups requirement conversations, original runs, revisions and comparisons by recorded source. Expand related records to follow a task from draft to alternative plans. History loads 100 items at a time. Load earlier runs to continue. Text and tag filters apply to loaded items, with the scope shown in the interface. Organize with tags and notes Open “More → Notes and tags.” For a staffing task, add store-staffing and record the chosen scenario and next confirmation. Search #store-staffing in the sidebar. Information Suggested record Task category Tags for production, staffing or transport Decision Note the chosen plan and reason Next action Record data or rules awaiting confirmation Comparison Retain the comparison link and related runs Export and share “More → Export report (Markdown)” saves the problem, settings, result, formulation, code and notes. Excel and CSV support complete numerical analysis; see exports . Run and comparison pages have fixed links for members using the same service. Links open the corresponding saved record for discussion of concrete inputs and models. Run again or edit “Run again” uses the same statement and settings. “Edit and run” returns inputs to the editor. Select a current preset when executing again. Each new run is retained independently. Deleting one record leaves other related runs. Original comparison checkpoints follow their original record; revised runs retain their own inputs and results. Persistence and team use The service workspace retains history, presets and run state across normal restarts. Tags and notes form a shared case library. Administrators can back up the complete workspace using the configuration guide . Start a task with requirements or continue a saved one in plan conversation .

title: Examples and benchmarks
description: Start from built-in examples and explore public benchmark problems.
text: Homepage examples introduce the workflow; public problem collections expose different statements and structures. Load a problem into the editor, then run it with your configuration. Three introductory tasks Example Decision Changes to try Production Quantities per product Hours and minimum orders Staffing Employee-by-day assignments Availability and coverage Delivery assignment Vehicle-to-store matching Disable a route or change costs The homepage provides three interactive fixed cases. Quickstart includes the production statement, recording and data. OR-Tools supplies staffing code; CPMpy supplies assignment code. Download production data Use production.json or production.csv . Explain products, time units and resource capacities before running. Choose nonnegative integer quantities of A and B to maximize profit. Each resource has 8 hours. Processing data uses hours per unit. JSON usage rows identify resources and columns identify products. Public problem collections The library contains 2,033 statements across nine groups: Collection Count Collection Count NL4Opt 205 IndustryOR 99 NL4LP 178 ComplexOR 18 MAMO Easy 642 OptiBench 403 MAMO Complex 210 OptMATH 128 NL4COP 150 Statements use the OPT-Agent collection. Provenance and licenses are recorded in benchmark sources . Use a problem Choose a group and statement, read it, and load it into the editor. Select method and solver according to domains, constraints and objective. After solving, tag the source and export the model, code and result. For comparison, fix the data and preset and use method comparison . For tasks requiring additional data, develop fields and units in the requirements assistant . Build your own case library Prepare business attachments, record meanings and adopted rules in notes, and tag runs. Revisions and scenarios connect later changes, gradually forming reusable team cases.

title: Configure LLM presets
description: Connect model services and manage fixed presets and provider parameters.
text: A preset stores provider, endpoint, model ID, API key and request parameters. Modeling and conversation select it by name; the server uses its saved configuration. Add and select a preset Open “LLM presets,” choose a provider, enter model ID and key, and configure endpoint and display name as needed. Select the saved preset in run settings or conversation. Providers include OpenAI, Google Gemini, Kimi, GLM, OpenRouter, Alibaba Bailian, DeepSeek, Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible services. Self-hosted models can use compatible endpoints. Field Value Display name A recognizable name such as “Team modeling” Model ID Identifier accepted by the service Endpoint API endpoint for the selected protocol API key Credentials for that endpoint Advanced parameters Supported provider-specific JSON fields Server default preset Administrators configure .env to provide the first-listed env preset: LLM4OM_LLM_PROVIDER=openai_compatible LLM4OM_LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com/v1 LLM4OM_LLM_MODEL=your-model-id LLM4OM_LLM_API_KEY=your-api-key LLM4OM_LLM_NAME=Team model Replace placeholders and recreate the service. UI-added presets use the workspace's private configuration; the default is managed through server environment variables. DeepSeek and structured calls DeepSeek uses a dedicated client. TriVAL uses forced tool selection; configure the run preset as: { "thinking" : { "type" : "disabled" } } The conversation thinking toggle controls that conversation's replies and is retained there. Modeling tools read run presets. Other providers use fields supported by their client integrations. OpenRouter and advanced parameters OpenRouter uses a dedicated integration. An example reasoning setting is: { "reasoning" : { "effort" : "high" } } Advanced fields are validated at submission; use dedicated fields for model, key and common options. Expand request errors for details. Failed saves retain entered form values. Change configuration and inspect usage Presets are fixed configurations. Delete and re-add to change parameters, obtaining a new ID. Select an available preset when running an older plan again. Historical runs retain their configuration summaries and results. The preset dialog shows daily usage. Administrators manage shared quotas and concurrency . Credentials stay in server-private files; records retain display configuration and usage. Resolve connection issues For 401, inspect credentials and provider. For 404, inspect endpoint and model ID. For tool errors, inspect structured-output support and advanced fields. Run a small Direct example first, then check the validation or conversation workflow you need.

checks"] Code --> Solver["Solver computation"] Solver --> Review["Substitute actual results into business rules"] Semantic checks interpret “each employee works at most five days.” Formulation checks require a sum for each employee. Code checks inspect indices and domains. The solver determines feasibility and optimality for the submitted model. Repair loops also differ. Some read only execution errors, others review the problem, and others backtranslate individual constraints. Compare trigger conditions and return points by inspecting their trigger conditions and return points. Read different workflows on one example For the production problem, Direct generates formulation and code before solving. Feedback Repair adds a review after solving. TriVAL creates semantic, formulation and code validation artifacts. Open the worked examples to follow the same rule through those stages. Quickstart provides the statement, data and recording. Method comparison provides side-by-side runs. What determines call cost Direct uses one modeling call. Feedback Repair without repairs uses two calls and one solve. Component methods scale with rule count; validation methods scale with failed checks and returns. AutoFormulation's candidate sampling has a substantially larger default budget. There is no reliable universal time per problem. Provider latency, attachment size, output length and mathematical difficulty all matter. The platform records actual calls, usage and elapsed time; parameter tables come from current presets. Problem scope and combinations OptiMUS, CoE, OptiTree, OR-LLM-Agent, AutoFormulation and SAC-Opt currently target LP/MILP. Other methods run according to the chosen model, library and backend. All nine libraries can be selected, but actual mathematics must fit the library and backend. For example, CPMpy has no continuous variables, OSQP does not solve integer programs, and Ipopt does not certify global optimality for general nonconvex models. Method and solver selection must both fit. Make comparisons informative Fix the problem, attachments, LLM preset, library, backend and limits, then vary one factor. Record rule coverage, domains, actual solutions, solver status, validation status, call count and solve count. One run on one problem can reveal differences, not establish a stable ranking. Retain failures: they help decide whether to clarify requirements, improve data descriptions or change checking workflows. See method and LLM comparison for the UI workflow.

title: Direct
description: Generate the mathematical model and solver code in one LLM call.
text: Direct sends the problem, data description and modeling-library contract to the LLM in one request. The reply contains a formulation and complete code. The platform executes the code and calls a real solver. This short workflow is useful for a first attempt and as a baseline for other methods. What the method does A solver cannot consume a business description directly. Direct translates the description into variables, an objective and constraints, then translates those expressions into code. Both translations happen in one reply. The formulation and code are followed by actual solver execution. Consider two products. A and B earn 3 and 2 per unit. They use 2 and 1 cutting hours, and 1 and 2 finishing hours. Each resource has 8 hours available. Products must be whole units. max ⁡ 3 A + 2 B s.t. 2 A + B ≤ 8 , A + 2 B ≤ 8 , A , B ∈ Z ≥ 0 . \max\;3A+2B\quad\text{s.t.}\quad2A+B\le8,\;A+2B\le8,\;A,B\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}. max 3 A + 2 B s.t. 2 A + B ≤ 8 , A + 2 B ≤ 8 , A , B ∈ Z ≥ 0 ​ . The critical choices are the integer domain, resource coefficients, units and maximization direction. Read 2. Generate 3. Compute 4. Check 1. Read Separate decisions from inputs. Profits and processing times are parameters; quantities are decisions. Profit (3, 2); cutting (2, 1); finishing (1, 2); capacity (8, 8) Quantities must be nonnegative integers. 2. Generate One reply supplies the formulation and build_model(data). Code must read full attachments even when their preview is truncated. Variables: A, B are nonnegative integers Objective: max 3A + 2B Constraints: 2A + B ≤ 8; A + 2B ≤ 8 3. Compute Code returns a native model. The platform calls a compatible backend; the LLM does not invent numerical answers. Integer optimum: A = 3, B = 2, objective 13 Cutting: 8 / 8; finishing: 7 / 8 4. Check Results retain the model, code and computed plan together for export, discussion and revision. Result: A = 3, B = 2, objective 13 Next: export CSV or revise cutting capacity to 10 hours. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. How to assess a result Check problem to formulation, formulation to code, then the values. Here, 2×3+2=8 , 3+2×2=7 and 3×3+2×2=13 . The formulation, code and values remain available in one run. Check that “at least” becomes ≥ and “at most” becomes ≤ . Check whether a rule applies per day, per product or across the whole plan. The integer optimum is 13. Download plan CSV Reset A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. Calls, stopping and when to use it The modeling stage uses one LLM call. Direct has no internal repair loop for reply format, execution or semantic errors. Incomplete replies fail before execution; execution failures retain feedback. Later platform explanations can make additional calls. Start with Direct for a clear problem and a quick first model. Use Feedback Repair for review after solving, TriVAL for validation at several levels, or BIND when binding large structured attachments is the central issue. Platform implementation and comparison This project maintains Direct and its shared Feedback Repair generator. It is not restricted to linear problems, although the library and backend must support the expressions used. Keep the problem, attachments, LLM preset and solver fixed when comparing workflows. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Direct has no method-specific preset parameters. Parameter definitions

title: Feedback Repair
description: Review the solved model against the problem and repair specific errors.
text: Feedback Repair adds execution, review against the original problem and targeted repair to Direct. It addresses a common failure: code runs and the solver reports optimality, but a business rule was translated incorrectly. Why review after a successful solve Suppose production requires at least 3 units of B, but the code says B <= 3 . The solver can return (3, 2) with objective 13. This is correct for the wrong model and violates the requirement. Fixing Python exceptions cannot detect it. The reviewer reads the problem, formulation, code, execution feedback and available conflict evidence. It checks coefficients, domains, constraint directions and data binding, then accepts or identifies a repair. First model 2. Review 3. Repair and solve 4. Accept or report 1. First model Assume generation reverses the demand constraint. The solver does not read the business description and can still report optimality. Required: B ≥ 3 Hypothetical error: B ≤ 3 Wrong-model optimum: A = 3, B = 2, objective 13 2. Review Name the mismatch. The mismatch becomes specific repair feedback. Decision: repair Reason: a minimum became an upper bound; B = 2 violates B ≥ 3. 3. Repair and solve Restore B ≥ 3, preserve the other requirements and execute the revised code. 2A + B ≤ 8; A + 2B ≤ 8; B ≥ 3 Integer optimum: A = 2, B = 3, objective 12 4. Accept or report The lower objective is the cost of satisfying the requirement. Accept after review, or retain artifacts and report an unresolved error when the budget ends. Original objective: 13. With B ≥ 3: 12. Both models and results remain available. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. What should be repaired Feedback Appropriate response Syntax error or invalid return object Repair from execution feedback Whole products modeled as continuous Restore integers and solve again Genuine demand and resource conflict Retain reviewed infeasibility and original requirements Time limit with a feasible incumbent Save status and available incumbent No objective for a satisfaction problem Check whether finding a satisfying assignment was intended Budget and final artifacts At most three repairs are shared across format, execution and modeling errors. A run without repair uses two LLM calls and one solve. Later explanations can add calls. An incomplete later reply preserves the last formulation, code and result actually executed. The platform does not choose an earlier model for its attractive objective. A failed or unparseable review also preserves computation and records the failure. Use it for a short workflow with review after execution. For layered validation, see TriVAL . For constraint backtranslation and frozen accepted components, see SAC-Opt . title: TriVAL
description: Validate semantics, formulation and code, with revisions across stages.
text: TriVAL separates three questions: was the problem understood correctly, does the formulation express that understanding, and does the code implement the formulation? Each level has construction, validation and revision. A code-stage finding can send the workflow back to the formulation. What each level checks Level Artifacts Example failure Revision Semantics Facts, ambiguities and resolutions Interpreting coverage per shift as a daily total Extract facts again or revise ambiguity resolutions Formulation Parameters, indices, variables, objective and constraints Missing per-shift coverage or reversing a minimum Revise locally or rebuild the formulation Code Native model code and execution evidence Wrong indices, domains or implementation Repair code, or return to the formulation if that is the cause This distinction puts repair where the error originated. Code that faithfully implements a wrong formulation will not improve through syntax fixes alone. CCheck{"Code validation and attribution"} CCheck -->|Code error and retry allowed| Code CCheck -->|Formulation error| Form CCheck -->|Passed or limit reached| Finish["Keep results and report unpassed stages"] FOLLOW THE EXAMPLE ← Play → 1. Semantic facts 2. Formulation 3. Execute and attribute 4. Report separately 1. Semantic facts Separate profits, processing times, resource limits and whole-unit requirements. An additional requirement of at least 3 units of B must remain a demand fact. Facts: whole products; 8 hours of each resource; B at least 3. Check interpretation: unit net profit and processing hours per unit. 2. Formulation Parameter/index, variable, objective and constraint experts construct in parallel. A selector assembles the formulation, which is checked against the facts. max 3A + 2B 2A + B ≤ 8; A + 2B ≤ 8; B ≥ 3 A, B are nonnegative integers 3. Execute and attribute If code omits B ≥ 3 but the formulation includes it, repair code. If the formulation also omits it, return to that level. Implementation omission → repair build_model(data) Formulation omission → revise formulation, then regenerate code The routes address different causes. 4. Report separately The correct integer optimum is 12. The final record shows numerical results and each stage's validation status. Solver evidence: A = 2, B = 3, objective 12 Record semantic / formulation / code validation separately Stage feedback records the final validation decision. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. How validation failures are routed Semantic checks distinguish faithful facts, relevant ambiguities and consistent resolutions. Faulty facts or ambiguity identification cause extraction again; inconsistent resolutions return to ambiguity resolution. Formulation checks can request partial revision or a new construction by the experts. Code is executed before code validation. Attribution to the formulation sends the outer workflow back to that level. An upstream stage can proceed with its latest artifacts after reaching its limit. The platform reports each unpassed stage at exit. Reading a run effectively Choose a rule that is easy to misinterpret and follow it through facts, formulation and code. For “each employee works at most five days,” check for an employee index with a separate constraint for each employee. Then inspect whether later artifacts actually address the validator's finding. The run retains solver values and stage validation feedback. Comparisons can inspect status, failed stages, revisions and actual call usage. Requirements and budget Select TriVAL and a library/backend supporting the intended mathematics. Each stage allows at most five validations; code execution allows twenty attempts. Total LLM use depends on nodes and return paths. For DeepSeek, forced tool choice requires thinking mode to be disabled in the preset: {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}} . See LLM presets . Related methods and implementation Feedback Repair reviews the model after solving; TriVAL moves checks into separate levels. SAC-Opt focuses on the consistency of backtranslated constraint code. The platform ports the pinned SCUT-EIPI/TriVAL implementation , retaining its graph, nodes, prompts and loops. It supplies the LLM and sandbox, maps input and reports unresolved validation at exit. title: OptiMUS 0.3
description: Extract parameters, objectives and constraints, then assemble component code.
text: OptiMUS 0.3 constructs a model component by component. It extracts parameters, objectives and constraints, formulates and codes individual components, then assembles and executes them. Intermediate artifacts make a long generation task easier to inspect. From rules to components “Only 8 cutting hours” is a business rule; 2A+B≤8 is its formulation; a native Constraint is its implementation. OptiMUS keeps these stages visible so readers can follow changes in meaning. Objectives and constraints are handled separately. Constraints receive redundancy and confidence checks. A low-confidence item can be retained, removed or modified. These are LLM judgments: check whether removal eliminates a duplicate or loses a distinct requirement. Parameters and rules 2. Check components 3. Assemble code 4. Execute and debug 1. Parameters and rules Identify profit, resource consumption and capacities as parameters. Two resources are not duplicates merely because both capacities equal 8. Profit: A=3, B=2 C1: cutting capacity 8, consumption (2,1) C2: finishing capacity 8, consumption (1,2) 2. Check components Repeated wording can be removed. Cutting and finishing have different coefficients and remain separate constraints. C1 → 2A + B ≤ 8 C2 → A + 2B ≤ 8 Preserve nonnegative integer domains. 3. Assemble code Components enter one build_model(data). Names, indices and parameters must agree across components. setup + variables + C1 + C2 + objective + return model Generated code builds; the platform solves. 4. Execute and debug The correct model gives A=3, B=2 and objective 13. If debugging occurs, check that changes preserve component meaning. At most 3 execution/debug attempts Infeasible or unbounded statuses can also trigger debugging. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Parameter data and confidence An attached params.json in the upstream format supplies parameters directly. Otherwise the method extracts them, including values, from the problem. An unknown business quantity must not become an invented fixed parameter. Constraint confidence uses five-point judgments with bounded retries. Low-confidence items receive further feedback deciding retention, removal or revision. The process retains those decisions and the updated list. How its repair differs Execution debugging treats optimality as success and also preserves explicitly local optimality from compatible backends. Infeasible and unbounded models can therefore enter debugging. Feedback Repair instead permits a reviewed, genuinely infeasible model to end normally. When infeasibility is plausible, check whether debugging changes a hard requirement. For checking code against individual constraint meanings, see SAC-Opt . Scope and reading a run The current method targets LP/MILP. Follow a rule through parameters, description, formulation, code and execution. More rules require more component calls. Defaults use temperature 1.0 and at most three execution/debug attempts. RAG and interactive human confirmation are not enabled. title: Chain-of-Experts
description: A conductor selects experts in sequence before a reducer produces the model.
text: Chain-of-Experts (CoE) asks a conductor to select experts in sequence. Later experts read earlier comments; a reducer produces the final model and code. Each comment enters the pool available to later roles. How comments affect the next step The conductor chooses among seven expert roles. Each expert sees the problem and the current comment pool, so later comments can extend or correct earlier ones. The default selects three experts per trial before reduction. Each expert uses its role prompt and current comment pool with the run's selected LLM preset. title: OptiTree
description: Match a problem type in a tree, retrieve guidance and generate code.
text: OptiTree searches a hierarchy of problem types before generating code. It makes “recognize the structure, then borrow a relevant modeling pattern” an explicit part of the workflow. What the type tree provides Transportation, assignment and staffing descriptions can share variable and constraint structures. The tree provides reasoning templates, not complete answers. Costs, indices, capacities and special rules must still come from the current problem. Matching starts at the Mixed Integer Programming root and selects only among the current node's children. The deepest matched node's full entry becomes context for generation. The process retains the matching path and retrieved entry. The actual matching path depends on the bundled tree and LLM decisions. Decisions: shipment quantities from warehouses to stores. Inputs: unit costs, warehouse supply, store demand. 2. Use the template A template can suggest indexed x[i,j], but the current wording determines whether supply and demand require equality or inequality. x[i,j] ≥ 0 Warehouse: sum_j x[i,j] ≤ supply[i] Store: sum_i x[i,j] ≥ demand[j], if required by the problem 3. Generate and execute Use the retrieved entry together with current data. Template example values must not replace user data. Check warehouse/store indices and cost-matrix orientation. Special business rules still need explicit constraints. 4. Handle no match Stop at the current node if no valid deeper type exists. Do not invent a classification. Inspection repairs execution failures. Unknown type / missing judgment / repeated path → stop descent At most 4 code inspections. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Why a broader match can be useful A specific but wrong type can impose the wrong structure. Treating divisible transport as one-to-one assignment can invent a restriction against split shipments. A broader match supplies general guidance while leaving details to the problem. Read the path, retrieved entry and final formulation together. The process shows the path and entry; the final model shows selected variables and constraints. Scope and related methods The current workflow targets LP/MILP, uses temperature 0 and permits four code inspections. Use it to study the effect of type retrieval. For component construction see OptiMUS ; for searching multiple complete candidates see AutoFormulation . title: OR-LLM-Agent
description: Build the formulation first, then generate, execute and recheck code.
text: OR-LLM-Agent builds a formulation before generating and executing code. Its main round, infeasibility check and recheck have separate budgets, allowing execution feedback to inform later modeling decisions. Why separate formulation and code A separate formulation gives readers a checkpoint without having to recover business meaning from Python. When execution fails, inspect whether code deviates from the formulation or the formulation itself needs revision. In transport, establish warehouse supply limits, store demand and the cost objective first. A transposed cost matrix is an implementation issue; reversed demand inequalities require formulation review. Locate runtime errors If cost[j][i] causes an index error, use the data orientation in execution feedback to repair indexing. Hypothetical error: costs indexed store-first. Actual data: warehouse rows, store columns. 3. Interpret the result Supply below hard demand can be genuinely infeasible. Distinguish a data conflict from a modeling error. Total supply 10, hard demand 12 → potentially genuine infeasibility. Do not invent permission for shortages merely to obtain a plan. 4. Check code versions Upstream round behavior can leave the final proposed repair unexecuted. Numerical results must stay attached to executed code. Intermediate artifact: latest repair proposal Numerical result: last actually executed model These are not one verified result. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Separate attempt budgets The preset assigns main 3, infeasibility 1 and recheck 2 attempts. Repairs use copied conversations; only the final code returns to the main conversation. Read each round together with its actual execution record. Difference from Chat Agent “Agent” here names a fixed modeling method. Chat Agent is the user-facing optimization conversation. It can call Direct, TriVAL or other methods and handles explanations, plan selection and scenarios. Selecting OR-LLM-Agent does not itself open a persistent conversation. Locate the last actual execution first; inspect its code, status, objective and variables before reading later repair suggestions. Final repair proposals and actual executions retain their respective artifacts. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. title: ORThought
description: Write a reasoning path, formulation and code, then debug execution errors.
text: ORThought asks the LLM to state a modeling path in an expert-like order, then provide the formulation and code. The path is retained so readers can understand why variables, objectives and constraints were chosen. What a useful modeling path explains Useful explanations name concrete choices: “whole products require integer quantities” or “processing hours add across products, so capacity is consumption times quantity.” Generic steps such as “analyze, model, optimize” do not explain these decisions. The current workflow uses the upstream formalized mode and outputs a modeling path, formulation and code. The process view retains this explanation as a separate solution_path artifact. Identify decisions 2. Explain expressions 3. Check execution 4. Read back results 1. Identify decisions Separate production decisions from known inputs. Decide production quantities A and B. Profit, processing times and capacity are given parameters. 2. Explain expressions Connect each expression to its business meaning instead of listing unexplained formulae. Whole units → nonnegative integer A, B Additive hours → 2A+B≤8, A+2B≤8 Total profit → max 3A+2B 3. Check execution If code cannot obtain a solver status, debugging reads the problem, formulation, code and actual error. Execution error → at most 3 code-debug attempts Valid infeasible status → no debugging solely for infeasibility 4. Read back results The correct integer optimum is 13. Substitute actual values into resource expressions to check the explanation. A=3, B=2 Cutting 8; finishing 7; profit 13 Explanation must agree with these actual values. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Execution repair versus semantic checking Code that cannot obtain a solver status enters debugging, up to three times. Successfully executed code returning infeasibility does not trigger debugging simply for lacking a feasible solution. This differs from OptiMUS . For explicit review against the problem see Feedback Repair ; for layered validation see TriVAL . When to use it and how to read it Use it when a retained modeling explanation helps learning and inspection. The method is not uniformly limited to linear models, but the selected library and backend still constrain supported mathematics. The saved path, formulation, code and values can be read together. Source and platform adaptation The platform ports the formalized workflow from the pinned ORThought implementation . It returns native models, executes in the sandbox and retains solution_path . title: LLMOPT
description: Construct a five-part formulation and route corrections to the affected stage.
text: LLMOPT connects language and code through a five-part formulation: Sets, Parameters, Variables, Objective and Constraints. After execution, self-correction judges the formulation and code separately and returns to the affected stage. How five elements locate errors The structure separates objects, known quantities, decisions, goals and requirements. Indices, units and domains have explicit places, making it easier to distinguish a modeling error from an implementation error. Element Production example Sets Products P={A,B}; resources R={cutting,finishing} Parameters Profit p, consumption matrix a, capacity b Variables Nonnegative integer quantities x[p] Objective Maximize title: AutoFormulation
description: Search candidate components and rank complete models with MCTS and comparisons.
text: AutoFormulation searches a tree of modeling components. It checks, deduplicates and ranks candidates, explores complete models with Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS), then selects a solved candidate through pairwise ranking. What is being searched Tree levels are parameters, decision variables, objective, equality constraints and inequality constraints. A root-to-leaf path is a complete model. Integer versus continuous production quantities, for example, are different variable choices affecting all later components. The search concerns interpretations of the problem. It is not simply choosing the production plan with the largest profit. Objectives from models obeying different rules cannot directly establish which interpretation is correct. Build candidates 2. Select a path 3. Establish comparisons 4. Select final model 1. Build candidates Equivalent notation should be deduplicated, while invalid components need checking. Different wording alone should not create distinct models. Candidate 1: nonnegative integer A, B Candidate 2: nonnegative integer x[p], p∈{A,B} These may differ only in notation. 2. Select a path UCT balances promising and underexplored paths. A complete path must be assembled and solved before becoming a solved candidate. Parameters → variables → objective → equalities → inequalities Each complete candidate has its own code and execution result. 3. Establish comparisons The first 3 solved models become baselines with reward 0.5. Later candidates are compared against baselines in both orders. Compare each candidate with baselines in both orders. Return comparison win rates as search rewards. 4. Select final model Bradley–Terry ranking selects the final solved model. Rankings are model judgments; readers still inspect domains and rules. Output: selected formulation, code and actual solver result. Equivalent candidates can leave one complete model, with no meaningful competition. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Equivalence and reward Parameters use a mode, variable candidates use repeated LLM grouping, and other expressions use symbolic SymPy/Z3 scripts for equivalence. Generated checking scripts run in the sandbox, not the host process. UCT uses exploration weight w_exp=1 and node-reward weight lambda_cte=0.5 . Repeated judgments in both comparison orders reduce dependence on a single reply or order. These judgments produce relative candidate preferences. Why the budget is much larger Defaults sample 8 completions per node, retain 3 candidates, use 5 ranking completions and run 16 rollouts. Initial tree construction can need about 540 completions; a later comparison can need about 30. Pruning reduces actual use. Its default run limits reach 20,000 LLM calls, 1,000 solves and 6 hours. Check deployment limits first. Parameters are changed in deployment presets, not through a per-run UI control. When it is useful Use it for LP/MILP candidate-modeling and search research, especially when inspecting structural alternatives. Explicit units, indices and field meanings reduce unhelpful candidates. For one inspectable first model with a smaller call budget, start with Direct or Feedback Repair . Source and platform adaptation Based on the pinned AutoFormulator implementation and ICML 2025 paper . The platform retains construction, MCTS and ranking, supplies sandboxed native-library code, bounds unparseable-comparison retries and fixes the reversed two-candidate comparison direction. Detailed differences are recorded in the source documentation. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. title: SAC-Opt
description: Extract semantic anchors and selectively repair constraints after backtranslation.
text: SAC-Opt preserves business meaning as semantic anchors, translates constraint code back into language, and compares that translation with the anchors. Failed constraints are repaired selectively; accepted components are frozen. Why read code backwards “Each employee works at most five days” requires summing over dates. Summing over employees can instead mean “at most five employees per day.” Both programs may execute while expressing different rules. The backtranslator reads constraint code and context to state its expressed rule. A comparator checks that translation against the original semantic anchor and returns a pass or repair decision. Keep anchors 2. Backtranslate 3. Selective repair 4. Assemble and run 1. Keep anchors Define binary x[e,d] for employee e and date d. Preserve requirements with their quantifiers and index meanings. x[e,d] = 1 if employee e works on date d. C1: each employee works at most 5 days. C2: at least 3 employees each day. 2. Backtranslate Suppose C1 mistakenly sums over employees. The translation reveals that it actually limits daily headcount. Hypothetical error: for each d, sum(x[e,d] for e in E) ≤ 5 Translation: at most 5 employees each day. 3. Selective repair Repair C1's quantifier and summation direction. Freeze C2 if it passed, avoiding unrelated rewrites. Repair C1: for each e, sum(x[e,d] for d in D) ≤ 5 Freeze C2: for each d, sum(x[e,d] for e in E) ≥ 3 4. Assemble and run Assemble checked components and execute the complete model. Preserve an explicit unresolved status if semantic checks exhaust their budget. Semantic consistency: recorded per constraint Executability: checked on the complete program Numerical plan: returned by the actual backend Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. From four anchor types to code Parameter and variable anchors capture symbols, shapes, units, domains and bounds. The current implementation retains parameters and variables with confidence scores above 3; low-confidence constraints receive further assessment. Code is generated as setup, objective and individual constraints, with component counts checked against anchors. Full attachments remain accessible through build_model(data) . Submitting several components together changes orchestration, not the unit of judgment: each constraint still receives its own consistency decision. Limits and failure interpretation Defaults allow five parse attempts, five semantic rounds and three full-program executions. Semantic checking and execution debugging are separate loops: one checks meaning, the other handles runtime failures. A repair produced after the final failed comparison cannot be presented as independently passed. The platform keeps unresolved failures alongside actual solver results. Inspect both the failed constraints and the code associated with the numerical result. When to consider this workflow Use it for LP/MILP problems with many rules, fragile indices or quantifiers, and a need to inspect individual constraints. It does not judge model quality from objective values alone. Compared with TriVAL , its focus is anchor-to-constraint-code consistency. Compared with Feedback Repair , repair is more granular. Platform implementation and sources This is an independent implementation of the published algorithm , using prompts written by this project. The pinned reference is Forrest-Stone/SAC-Opt . The platform retains anchors, blind backtranslation and selective repair, with batched components and native-model contracts. The published source records the component and contract adaptations. title: BIND
description: Show data structure to the LLM and read complete attachments during execution.
text: BIND separates understanding data structure from reading complete values. The LLM sees fields, types and sizes; generated code reads the full JSON/CSV during execution. This addresses truncated previews, long-table transcription and data-binding errors. Why structure can be enough Model structure often does not depend on every individual value. A transport model needs to know that costs form a warehouse-by-store matrix and demand is indexed by store. It need not copy every matrix entry into a prompt and back into code. Structure does not replace meaning. The problem must still explain whether capacity means hours, units or vehicle load. Field names alone cannot reliably specify all business rules. 1. Prepare data 2. Provide structure 3. Bind at execution 4. Check and repair 1. Prepare data Upload structured data and explain units and index meanings in the problem. production.json profit: profit per unit, indexed by product usage: resource-by-product hours per unit capacity: available hours per resource 2. Provide structure Generation receives field structure, including nested and irregular shapes. profit: array[number], length 2 usage: array[array[number]], 2 rows capacity: array[number], length 2 3. Bind at execution Code parses complete file text from data and constructs expressions from those values. payload = json.loads(data['production.json']) profit = payload['profit'] usage = payload['usage'] capacity = payload['capacity'] 4. Check and repair Format and execution errors can trigger retries. Genuine infeasibility is a valid status, not permission to relax requirements. At most 3 generation/execution attempts. Check row/column meaning and units, not just successful parsing. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. A ready-to-use example { "products" : [ "A" , "B" ] , "profit" : [ 3 , 2 ] , "usage" : [ [ 2 , 1 ] , [ 1 , 2 ] ] , "capacity" : [ 8 , 8 ] } Describe it as: “ usage[r][p] gives hours of resource r per unit of product p. capacity[r] is available hours. Choose nonnegative integer quantities to maximize total profit without exceeding any resource.” The correct result is A=3, B=2, objective 13. The data editor example demonstrates editing while preserving original result snapshots. Supported inputs and information boundaries JSON and CSV are supported; the frontend converts Excel to CSV. CSV headers and row widths are checked before LLM calls. Heterogeneous nested JSON is not presented as a rectangular matrix. Without attachments, the method uses the problem directly. It adds no PDF or image parser. Generation receives schema; execution reads complete attachments. Later feedback can include actual objectives and decision values. When to use it and what to check Use it for structured data too large to transcribe conveniently when rules are clear. Inspect file names, fields, matrix orientation, units and iteration over all records. For semantic review of complex rules, compare with Feedback Repair or TriVAL . Source and platform adaptation Based on schema offload and the default agentic path in the pinned Text2Opt-Bench implementation . User attachments replace benchmark data; reference-optimum and model-size scoring are removed. The platform returns a formulation and native model code, repairing according to actual execution status. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 0 top_p 1 max_rounds 3 Parameter definitions

title: OptiMind
description: Combine public problem-type hints with multi-turn solver feedback.
text: OptiMind combines public problem-type hints with multi-turn solver feedback. A successful solve still produces feedback, allowing another revision or a final textual answer that ends the trajectory. What the hint library provides Type hints highlight common modeling mistakes. In traveling salesperson models, one incoming and one outgoing edge per city can still produce separate subtours; additional constraints must enforce a single tour. The public library currently contains only TravelingSalesman, with six error/hint pairs. Classification selects a public type or no match. Unmatched problems receive general checking guidance. code"] Generate --> Solve["Actually execute and solve"] Solve --> Feedback["Return status, objective and variables"] Feedback --> Decision{"Next model reply"} Decision -->|Revised code and budget left| Generate Decision -->|Code-free final answer after execution| Finish["Keep last executed model"] Decision -->|Generation limit reached| Finish FOLLOW THE EXAMPLE ← Play → 1. Match hints 2. Generate and solve 3. Check success too 4. End one trajectory 1. Match hints Traveling salesperson problems can use public specialist hints. Other types use general checks when no public entry matches. Example: visit every city once and return to the start. Reminder: in-degree/out-degree constraints do not eliminate separate subtours. 2. Generate and solve The generator turns hints into constraints; the process retains both the hint and generated formulation. Inspect binary edges, degree constraints and subtour elimination. Actual solver execution provides the numerical result. 3. Check success too Read selected edges even after optimality. Separate cycles identify a connectivity rule to inspect. Two disjoint cycles → inspect connectivity constraints. Faithful model and result → final answer can end the run. 4. End one trajectory The default follows one trajectory without majority voting. A code-free final answer preserves the last executed result. At most 5 generations; temperature 0.6; top_p 0.95. Textual completion does not replace execution. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Revision and stopping Feedback includes successful as well as failed statuses, objectives and values. Revised code continues the generate–execute–feedback loop. After a valid execution, a final reply without code can stop it. Without any valid execution, a code-free reply is not completion; code is requested again within the budget. Final numbers come from the last executed model, not the final prose. Comparing related workflows Feedback Repair has an explicit accept-or-repair review. OptiMind centers on hints and continuing feedback within one trajectory. OptiTree retrieves entries from a hierarchical type tree, a different source and use of guidance. Use it to inspect the effect of public hints. The current registry does not impose a uniform linear-only restriction; library, backend and hint scope still apply. Weights, orchestration and specialist hints are separate experimental conditions. Public scope and platform implementation Based on the pinned Microsoft OptiGuide/optimind implementation . The platform preserves public hint files, adds optional type matching and supplies native-model contracts and actual solver feedback. The public hint files and adaptation are available in source. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. title: Choose a library and solver
description: Understand the nine libraries, backend capabilities, AUTO and availability.
text: Choose the mathematics first, then the modeling library and backend. A library expresses a model; a backend computes it. Selecting a library does not make every problem compatible with every solver. Start with variables and constraints Structure Mathematics Combinations to inspect Divisible quantities and linear expressions LP Pyomo / PuLP with compatible HiGHS, CBC or other engines Whole units, switches or locations with linear constraints MILP Pyomo, PuLP, gurobipy, PySCIPOpt, coptpy or OR-Tools mathematical programming Scheduling, logic, exclusion and finite domains CP / SAT-style discrete constraints CPMpy with OR-Tools, or OR-Tools CP-SAT Convex quadratic losses, norms or cones Convex QP / conic programming CVXPY with compatible OSQP, Clarabel, SCS or other engines Smooth nonlinear continuous decisions NLP CasADi with Ipopt or another suitable native path Routing, flow, assignment or knapsack Specialized combinatorial structure The corresponding OR-Tools interface Business names alone do not establish compatibility. Staffing can be MILP; production can include nonlinear losses. Domains and expression structure determine the mathematical requirements. title: Pyomo
description: Express algebraic models and connect compatible native backends.
text: Pyomo expresses optimization in a form close to mathematical notation. Products, factories and dates become index sets; objectives and constraints use those indices, making business rules easier to map to code. Start with the mathematics Choose whole-unit quantities A and B, maximize 3A+2B , and enforce cutting 2A+B≤8 and finishing A+2B≤8 . The integer optimum is A=3, B=2, objective 13. If quantities are genuinely divisible, continuous domains give A=B=8/3 and objective 40/3. The selected domain is recorded in the model. Complete platform code import pyomo.environ as pyo def build_model ( data ): model = pyo.ConcreteModel() model.products = pyo. Set (initialize=[ "A" , "B" ]) profit = { "A" : 3 , "B" : 2 } model.x = pyo.Var(model.products, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers) model.profit = pyo.Objective( expr= sum (profit[p] * model.x[p] for p in model.products), sense=pyo.maximize, ) model.cutting = pyo.Constraint(expr= 2 *model.x[ "A" ] + model.x[ "B" ] <= 8 ) model.finishing = pyo.Constraint(expr=model.x[ "A" ] + 2 *model.x[ "B" ] <= 8 ) return model There is no solve() call. The platform selects a backend, solves and reads named variables. For attachments, parse complete parameters with json.loads(data['production.json']) ; see BIND . title: gurobipy / Gurobi
description: Use Gurobi's native Python models, matrix API and conflict evidence.
text: gurobipy constructs native Gurobi models. It suits workflows using native variables, constraints, matrix expressions and diagnostics. Actual solving requires a usable Gurobi license in the execution environment. Model and engine A gurobipy Model belongs to Gurobi; it uses the native Gurobi engine. Scalar and matrix APIs both construct gp.Model and can be chosen to match data structure. Production, transportation and location LP/MILP are common starting points. For quadratic, conic or other native expressions, also check the installed version, engine capability and modeling method scope. Complete production model import gurobipy as gp from gurobipy import GRB def build_model ( data ): model = gp.Model( "production" ) a = model.addVar(lb= 0 , vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name= "A" ) b = model.addVar(lb= 0 , vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name= "B" ) model.setObjective( 3 *a + 2 *b, GRB.MAXIMIZE) model.addConstr( 2 *a + b <= 8 , name= "cutting" ) model.addConstr(a + 2 *b <= 8 , name= "finishing" ) return model Do not call optimize() . Platform execution should give A=3, B=2 and objective 13. Matrix modeling with MVar still needs clear names, dimensions and row/column meanings. Review and export a plan Results show named variables, objective, status and actual backend. Inspect A and B directly in this example. Matrix variables are read by component indices, and complete exports support further analysis. Try it: resources, integers and infeasibility INTERACTIVE Cutting hours 8 Minimum B 0 3 4 5 Quantity domain Integer: whole units Continuous: divisible units A = 3, B = 2 · 13 Maximize 3A + 2B; 2A + B ≤ 8 and A + 2B ≤ 8. The integer optimum is 13. Download plan CSV Reset A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. Change capacities and demand in the example to see revised plans. Actual platform runs save the process, model and results together for inspection and comparison. Using IIS for infeasibility Add B≥5 : finishing A+2B≤8 already conflicts with nonnegative quantities. Supported linear Gurobi paths can produce an IIS identifying jointly inconsistent constraints or bounds. An IIS lists an irreducible set of conflicting constraints or bounds to help locate requirements for revision. Named constraints improve the connection to requirements; see infeasibility and conflicts . Licenses and common failures Distinguish missing licenses, environment mismatch, size restrictions and modeling errors. Containers use GRB_LICENSE_FILE for an offline license mounted read-only; see backends and licenses . Selection and references Choose it when a suitable Gurobi environment is available and native interfaces or conflict evidence matter. For initial linear-model learning without that license, use open backends through Pyomo or PuLP . See the Gurobi Python API .

title: OR-Tools
description: Use native linear, integer, constraint, routing and network-flow interfaces.
text: OR-Tools provides mathematical programming, constraint programming, routing and graph algorithms. The platform recognizes the returned native model and uses its corresponding solving path. Choose the native interface by task Interface Model structure Backend examples MPSolver / MathOpt / ModelBuilder Linear, integer and interface-supported mathematical programming Compatible SCIP, HIGHS and other engines CpModel / CP-SAT Finite integers, Booleans, scheduling and logic CP_SAT RoutingModel Vehicles, visits, capacities and time windows ROUTING Original Constraint Solver Finite-domain constraints and search CP Maximum / minimum-cost flow Network arcs, capacities, costs and supply MAX_FLOW, MIN_COST_FLOW Assignment / knapsack One-to-one matching and capacity-limited selection ASSIGNMENT, KNAPSACK_* Select OR-Tools and a backend in settings; code determines the API. The default mathematical-programming reference uses SCIP. HIGHS can use MathOpt. A complete CP-SAT staffing model Four employees each work one day. Monday and Tuesday each need two employees. x[e,d] indicates whether employee e works on day d; costs are in the matrix below. from ortools.sat.python import cp_model def build_model ( data ): costs = [[ 1 , 7 ], [ 2 , 8 ], [ 7 , 1 ], [ 8 , 2 ]] model = cp_model.CpModel() x = {(e, d): model.new_bool_var( f"work[ {e} , {d} ]" ) for e in range ( 4 ) for d in range ( 2 )} for e in range ( 4 ): model.add( sum (x[e, d] for d in range ( 2 )) == 1 ) for d in range ( 2 ): model.add( sum (x[e, d] for e in range ( 4 )) == 2 ) model.minimize( sum (costs[e][d] * x[e, d] for e in range ( 4 ) for d in range ( 2 ))) return model Choose CP_SAT . Employees 0 and 1 work Monday; 2 and 3 work Tuesday, for cost 6. Requiring employee 0 on Tuesday raises the optimum to 18. Use scenario comparison for independent staffing changes. title: CPMpy
description: Model discrete decisions with integer, Boolean and global constraints.
text: CPMpy expresses discrete decisions with finite-domain integers, Booleans and global constraints. Arrays fit employees, dates, machines and tasks; AllDifferent , Element and Cumulative express common rules directly. How global constraints simplify a model Three vehicles each serve one of three stores, with exactly one vehicle per store. Let destination[i] identify vehicle i's store. AllDifferent(destination) expresses distinct destinations; costs are indexed from each vehicle's cost row. Each variable has domain 0 through 2, with each value identifying a store. CPMpy passes these finite-domain expressions to a native backend. Complete assignment model import cpmpy as cp def build_model ( data ): cost = cp.cpm_array([[ 4 , 8 , 6 ], [ 7 , 3 , 9 ], [ 5 , 6 , 2 ]]) destination = cp.intvar( 0 , 2 , shape= 3 , name= "destination" ) model = cp.Model(cp.AllDifferent(destination)) model.minimize( sum (cost[i, destination[i]] for i in range ( 3 ))) return model The default backend is OR-Tools CP-SAT. The optimum assigns vehicles 0, 1 and 2 to stores 0, 1 and 2, for 4+3+2=9 . Adding destination[1] != 1 raises the optimum to 17.
