title: PuLP
description: Build linear and mixed-integer models with CBC or other native backends.
text: PuLP targets linear and mixed-integer programming. Variables, linear sums and inequalities suit production, transportation, budgets and allocation when relationships are linear. What linear means 3A+2B and 2A+B≤8 are linear because coefficients are known constants. A×B , A² and division by an unknown variable are not. Convex quadratic losses and norms can use libraries such as CVXPY, linked below. Binary decisions can still express switches in a linear model. With a valid capacity bound, production ≤ capacity × open links production to a binary opening decision because capacity is constant. Complete production model import pulp def build_model ( data ): model = pulp.LpProblem( "production" , pulp.LpMaximize) a = pulp.LpVariable( "A" , lowBound= 0 , cat= "Integer" ) b = pulp.LpVariable( "B" , lowBound= 0 , cat= "Integer" ) model += 3 *a + 2 *b, "profit" model += 2 *a + b <= 8 , "cutting" model += a + 2 *b <= 8 , "finishing" return model The expression without a comparison defines the objective; comparison expressions add constraints. Names must be unique. The platform calls CBC or the explicit compatible backend; generated code does not call model.solve() . Default backend and interfaces The default is PULP_CBC_CMD . Other backends are discovered through native listSolvers/getSolver , preserving Python, command-line and dynamic-library identifiers. Row-oriented algebra and column-oriented LpConstraintVar both return LpProblem . Choose a form matching the data organization. Review and revise results The example gives A=3, B=2 and objective 13. Results show variables, objective and actual backend. Export the full data or revise capacities and minimum demand from the saved plan. Try it: resources, integers and infeasibility INTERACTIVE Cutting hours 8 Minimum B 0 3 4 5 Quantity domain Integer: whole units Continuous: divisible units A = 3, B = 2 · 13 Maximize 3A + 2B; 2A + B ≤ 8 and A + 2B ≤ 8. The integer optimum is 13. Download plan CSV Reset A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. Change cutting capacity or minimum B in the example and download the current CSV. See revisions and scenario comparison for the platform workflow. Common issues and selection Specify cat="Integer" for whole quantities and cat="Binary" for switches. Inspect names, objective direction and every resource constraint. For variable-product expressions, select a library supporting the required structure. See Pyomo for broader algebraic modeling, CVXPY for convex norms and quadratic losses, or CPMpy for discrete logic and global constraints. API details are in the official PuLP documentation .

title: CVXPY
description: Model convex optimization and select a backend for its cones and domains.
text: CVXPY builds convex and related models with structured mathematical expressions. Native atoms for squared losses, norms, linear maps and cones suit fitting, allocation, portfolio weights and regularized optimization. A complete convex quadratic example Choose continuous (x,y) near target (1,2) , with nonnegative quantities and a total resource limit of 2: min ⁡ x , y ≥ 0 ( x − 1 ) 2 + ( y − 2 ) 2 s.t. x + y ≤ 2. \min_{x,y\ge0}(x-1)^2+(y-2)^2\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x+y\le2. min x , y ≥ 0 ​ ( x − 1 ) 2 + ( y − 2 ) 2 s.t. x + y ≤ 2. The optimum is (0.5,1.5) , objective 0.5. import cvxpy as cp def build_model ( data ): x = cp.Variable( 2 , nonneg= True , name= "allocation" ) objective = cp.Minimize(cp.sum_squares(x - [ 1.0 , 2.0 ])) return cp.Problem(objective, [cp. sum (x) <= 2 ]) Select CVXPY. OSQP supports this continuous convex quadratic objective with linear constraints. Return Problem ; the platform solves and reads its variable array. Explore resource changes Try convex optimization: the nearest feasible point INTERACTIVE Total resource limit 2 x = 0.5, y = 1.5 · 0.5 Minimize (x − 1)² + (y − 2)², subject to x + y ≤ 2 and x, y ≥ 0. A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. Increase the limit from 2 to 3 to move the solution toward the target. A line connects target and solution; the ellipse is an equal-objective contour around the target. Variable components map to x and y in array order. title: PySCIPOpt / SCIP
description: Use native SCIP for linear, integer and nonlinear constraints.
text: PySCIPOpt uses native SCIP models for linear, integer and nonlinear constraints. It suits models combining discrete choices with native nonlinear expressions. Expressing a nonlinear objective The native interface uses a linear objective. Introduce auxiliary t, constrain cost(x)≤t , and minimize t. This epigraph form preserves the cost while fitting the interface. The example minimizes squared distance to (1,2) under a resource limit of 2. Auxiliary loss represents that cost. Complete native model from pyscipopt import Model def build_model ( data ): model = Model( "allocation" ) x = model.addVar(name= "x" , lb= 0 , vtype= "C" ) y = model.addVar(name= "y" , lb= 0 , vtype= "C" ) loss = model.addVar(name= "loss" , lb= 0 , vtype= "C" ) model.addCons(x + y <= 2 , name= "resource" ) model.addCons((x- 1 )** 2 + (y- 2 )** 2 <= loss, name= "loss_definition" ) model.setObjective(loss, "minimize" ) return model SCIP should return values near x=0.5, y=1.5 and loss=0.5, read with numerical tolerances. Return Model; the platform performs solving. title: CasADi
description: Express smooth nonlinear models and understand plugin and local-solution semantics.
text: CasADi builds optimization problems with symbolic expressions and automatic differentiation. Opti organizes variables, objectives and constraints; Ipopt is a common path for smooth continuous nonlinear models. A complete nonlinear model This single-variable objective has two wells, allowing exploration of starting points and local results: min ⁡ − 2 ≤ x ≤ 2 ( x 2 − 1 ) 2 + 0.2 x . \min_{-2\le x\le2}\;(x^2-1)^2+0.2x. min − 2 ≤ x ≤ 2 ​ ( x 2 − 1 ) 2 + 0.2 x . import casadi as ca def build_model ( data ): model = ca.Opti() x = model.variable() model.minimize((x*x - 1 )** 2 + 0.2 *x) model.subject_to(model.bounded(- 2 , x, 2 )) model.set_initial(x, - 1.8 ) return model Select CasADi and Ipopt. Initial values, bounds and smooth expressions enter the solve. Results use native CasADi variable names; describe component meanings in the formulation. title: coptpy / COPT
description: Use the native COPT interface and check model and license requirements.
text: coptpy constructs native COPT models for LP, MILP, convex quadratic and supported conic optimization. Scalar and matrix APIs use the COPT engine. When native interfaces help Use it when a team already works with COPT and wants consistent native models and execution. Different libraries can express the same production model. Keep domains, capacities and coefficients fixed when comparing. Differences in speed or objective cannot be attributed to engines if the business models differ. Complete production model import coptpy as cp from coptpy import COPT def build_model ( data ): model = cp.Envr().createModel( "production" ) a = model.addVar(lb= 0 , vtype=COPT.INTEGER, name= "A" ) b = model.addVar(lb= 0 , vtype=COPT.INTEGER, name= "B" ) model.setObjective( 3 *a + 2 *b, COPT.MAXIMIZE) model.addConstr( 2 *a + b <= 8 , name= "cutting" ) model.addConstr(a + 2 *b <= 8 , name= "finishing" ) return model Return the model; the platform solves it. The integer optimum is A=3, B=2, objective 13. Indexed models can use addVars ; matrix APIs still require correct dimensions. Convex quadratic structure and integer domains Validate a small linear case first. Adding quadratic costs requires checking convexity and backend support. Integer decisions also require the appropriate mixed-integer capability. Try it: resources, integers and infeasibility INTERACTIVE Cutting hours 8 Minimum B 0 3 4 5 Quantity domain Integer: whole units Continuous: divisible units A = 3, B = 2 · 13 Maximize 3A + 2B; 2A + B ≤ 8 and A + 2B ≤ 8. The integer optimum is 13. Download plan CSV Reset A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. Changing the quantity domain changes the example's mathematics. The interaction shows the corresponding values and objective. Licensing and deployment COPT has a restricted small-scale noncommercial path under applicable conditions. Larger models or commercial use require the appropriate license. Deployment uses COPT_LICENSE_DIR with the specific license.dat and license.key files mounted read-only for the sandbox. Package installation, library loading and license validation are separate steps; see backends and licenses . Checking results and references Inspect engine, status, objective direction and decision values. Distinguish a retained feasible incumbent from proven optimality after a limit. Use hand calculations for small resource models and retain full models and exports for larger reviews. See the COPT Python documentation and installation and licensing guide .

Restart after dependency or license changes to discover again. Run a complete small model from the library guide to check the selected path. Configure commercial licenses Engine Environment variable Example file Gurobi GRB_LICENSE_FILE /opt/gurobi/gurobi.lic MOSEK MOSEKLM_LICENSE_FILE /opt/mosek/mosek.lic COPT COPT_LICENSE_DIR Directory with license.dat and license.key Prepare an offline, container-compatible license on the host. Mount identical absolute paths into app. Example compose.override.yaml : services: app: volumes: - /opt/gurobi/gurobi.lic:/opt/gurobi/gurobi.lic:ro - /opt/mosek/mosek.lic:/opt/mosek/mosek.lic:ro - /opt/copt/license.dat:/opt/copt/license.dat:ro - /opt/copt/license.key:/opt/copt/license.key:ro Set the corresponding .env variables and run docker compose up -d app . Workers mount the specified files read-only. Keep entries for the engines you use. Locate environment issues Error Inspect Executable missing Worker installation and PATH Plugin cannot load Native libraries, drivers and dependencies License path/host mismatch Paths, container compatibility and license contents Unsupported model type Domains, expressions and engine capabilities Model-size restriction License and intended model size Retain complete errors with engine information for inspection. See troubleshooting . Native references See Gurobi documentation , MOSEK client setup and COPT installation/licensing . Use solver selection for interfaces and mathematics.

Workers use disabled networking, read-only root filesystems, non-root execution and resource limits, then are removed. llm4om-data retains presets, history and runs. Shared access The workbench uses a shared workspace: members use presets, view runs and manage notes and records. Configure team IP access or an authenticated reverse proxy at the service entrance. The Docker socket grants app permission to create host containers; choose and configure the host accordingly. See configuration for defaults, quotas and concurrency. Domain and HTTPS Point a domain at the server and open ports 80/443. Set the actual domain in .env : LLM4OM_DOMAIN=llm4om.example.edu LLM4OM_PORT=127.0.0.1:8767 LLM4OM_TRUST_PROXY=1 Then run: docker compose --profile https up -d --build docker compose logs -f https Caddy obtains and stores certificates and forwards pages and live streams to app. LLM4OM_TRUST_PROXY=1 counts hourly usage by forwarded client address. Concurrency and resources Set active runs in compose.override.yaml , for example: services: app: command: [ "llm4om" , "serve" , "--workspace" , "/data" , "--port" , "8767" , "--jobs" , "8" ] LLM4OM_SANDBOX_JOBS separately controls all concurrent solves and checking scripts. Choose values according to model-service quotas and host resources. Update, migrate and back up Run git pull , then docker compose up -d --build for updates. Apply environment changes with docker compose up -d app . docker compose down stops services while retaining data volumes. To migrate a Python workspace, stop the target app, copy inputs into /data/ , then start. See backups for commands and backends for license mounts.

title: Configuration, usage and backups
description: Configure LLMs, concurrency, usage limits and persistent storage.
text: Configuration controls default models, concurrency, quotas and persistence. Compose uses .env and a data volume; Python services use environment variables and --workspace . Model and search settings Field Role LLM4OM_LLM_PROVIDER Default provider LLM4OM_LLM_BASE_URL Service endpoint LLM4OM_LLM_MODEL Actual model ID LLM4OM_LLM_API_KEY Service credentials LLM4OM_LLM_NAME Display name LLM4OM_LLM_EXTRA_BODY Provider-specific JSON LLM4OM_SEARCH_API_KEY Separate search credentials LLM4OM_SEARCH_BASE_URL Search endpoint DeepSeek presets can use their own search configuration; other providers use separate search credentials. See presets . Shared usage limits LLM4OM_DAILY_TOKENS=2000000 LLM4OM_RUNS_PER_HOUR=30 LLM4OM_SANDBOX_JOBS=4 TZ=Asia/Shanghai LLM4OM_TRUST_PROXY=1 Daily quotas count input plus output tokens per preset. Hourly limits count runs per client address. Zero or unset limits are unlimited. TZ=Asia/Shanghai resets daily usage at Beijing midnight. The preset dialog shows usage. At the daily cap, the next model call shows a quota message; choose another available preset or continue the following day. Saved results remain readable. queued. Four sandbox slots cover all solves and checks, including parallel AutoFormulation checks. Waiting counts toward run limits. One service process manages each workspace. Back up the workspace The volume stores presets, credentials, history and runs. Stop app to finish persistence, then copy: docker compose stop app docker compose cp app:/data ./llm4om-backup chmod -R go-rwx ./llm4om-backup docker compose start app Keep backups in access-controlled storage. For Python services, back up the selected --workspace directory. Restore or migrate docker compose stop app docker compose cp ./llm4om-backup/. app:/data/ docker compose start app To migrate Python history, substitute runs/web/. or the actual workspace. After startup, inspect presets and a historical run to confirm records and attachments. The service persists every ten seconds and at normal exit, writing a temporary file before renaming. Normal stop commands complete persistence of public steps and artifacts. Optional call tracing Set LANGSMITH_TRACING , LANGSMITH_API_KEY and LANGSMITH_PROJECT for external tracing. Enabled tracing sends problems, data and model replies to LangSmith while retaining local run records. See the repository's environment example and team deployment for HTTPS and service access.

title: CLI and Python
description: Run the same modeling workflows from the CLI or Python.
text: CLI and Python execute the same modeling graphs as the workbench. Use them for batches, saved states and integration. Prepare dependencies and Worker using installation , then select an LLM preset. Run one problem from the CLI Save the quickstart production statement as UTF-8 problem.txt . Use a preset in the workspace: uv run llm4om run --file problem.txt --workspace runs/web --method direct --language pyomo --solver highs --output result.json The terminal shows stages, formulation, code and result. result.json retains final state and steps for further processing. Attach data and select a preset uv run llm4om run --file problem.txt --data production.json --method bind --language pyomo --workspace runs/web --preset your-preset-id --output result.json Repeat --data for more files. Code reads text by original file name. --preset uses a saved workspace ID; omission selects the default. Download data from attachments . Option Purpose --problem / --file Inline statement or UTF-8 file --method ID such as feedback_repair or sac_opt --language ID such as pyomo, ortools or cvxpy --solver Native ID; omission uses AUTO --workspace / --preset Preset workspace and ID --output Save final JSON state Complete minimal Python call from llm4om import run_problem state = run_problem( "Produce nonnegative integer A and B with profits 3 and 2. " "Cutting: 2A+B<=8; finishing: A+2B<=8. Maximize total profit." , method= "direct" , language= "pyomo" , solver= "highs" , workspace= "runs/web" , explain= True , locale= "en" , ) print (state.get( "failure" ) or state.get( "solve" )) The returned state includes problem, configuration, formulation, code, solve and steps. explain=True adds a business explanation; locale sets its language. Supply complete data in Python from pathlib import Path from llm4om import run_problem state = run_problem( "Use production.json to choose nonnegative integer quantities and maximize profit. " "usage is resource-by-product hours per unit; capacity is available hours." , method= "bind" , language= "pyomo" , data={ "production.json" : Path( "production.json" ).read_text(encoding= "utf-8" )}, workspace= "runs/web" , ) print (state.get( "solve" , {}).get( "variables" )) data maps file names to text, matching workbench attachments. Supply model configuration explicitly Pass llm=LLMSettings(...) for script-defined service configuration and read credentials from environment variables. Fields are defined in LLMSettings . Method parameters come from presets. Async integrations can use lower-level run and Resources ; see the public Python module . Handle run state Read failure and solve.status before processing values. Steps locate model calls, execution and validation feedback. For browsable retained history, the workbench provides links, tags, notes and exports; see history .

title: Troubleshooting
description: Resolve connection, LLM, solver and result issues from the actual error.
text: Start with the failed stage and complete error. The following checks cover connections, model requests, execution, validation and recovery. Pages and service connections Symptom Check/action Local page unavailable Inspect docker compose ps and docker compose logs -f app Other devices cannot connect Check server IP, mapping, firewall and security group HTTPS certificate issue Check DNS, ports 80/443 and docker compose logs -f https Interrupted live progress Refresh the run link; inspect proxy streaming and server logs Python startup prints the listening address and workspace. Compose uses LLM4OM_PORT . Presets and model requests Error Action 401 Check key and provider 404 Check endpoint, protocol and model ID Structured-output/tool-choice error Inspect service tool support, method and advanced parameters DeepSeek with TriVAL Set {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}} in the run preset Quota message Check daily usage and select an available preset or continue next day Failed saves retain entered values. Follow preset configuration , then confirm with a small example. Execution environment and code For a missing Worker, run docker compose up -d --build , or uv run llm4om build-worker in Python setups. For Docker connection errors, inspect the service, socket permissions and DOCKER_SOCKET . For backend/license failures, read complete feedback and follow backend setup . Execution errors identify exceptions and stages. Locate file names, fields, indices, return objects or APIs, then rerun the appropriate repair workflow from the problem. Method validation and solver results TriVAL retains semantic, formulation and code validation; SAC-Opt retains per-constraint comparisons; Feedback Repair retains accept/repair reasons. Failure messages identify stages, with artifacts and executions in the process view. Open the relevant stage and compare feedback with its model/code version. Method articles provide stopping conditions, return paths and parameters for following the run. Infeasibility and native statuses Use conflict analysis when IIS/MUS evidence is available, then revise the relevant rules. For nonlinear paths, inspect starts, bounds and native feedback before computing further scenarios. Run information records time, calls and quotas. See configuration for limits and solvers for mathematical selection. Recovery and issue records Refresh reconnects conversations to active runs; open saved plans from cards or history. Retry original messages after stopping. Batch retries reuse saved scenarios and continue remaining work. Capture run link, method, library, backend, public preset configuration, failed stage, complete error and relevant problem text. These connect an issue to concrete inputs and execution. See maintenance for logs and backups.
